text:
ashok: Heads up - proposing a new 'bailout anchor' for per-org routing overrides. Emergency fallback that pins traffic to a safe model path and attaches an audit token. Want quick feedback before I open an RFC/PR.

katie: quick q — how is this different from the current escape-hatch? :thinking_face:

ashok: Main diffs: (1) override is bound to a signed audit token + TTL, (2) once issued it's immutable except through an org-admin console flow with 2FA + approval, (3) automatic telemetry rollup with structured reason tags for postop analysis.

ryan: do we need a new header? the current `x-org-route-token` isn't strongly authenticated today.

maria: recommend signed JWTs (short-lived) so proxies can verify without async calls to auth. HMAC is fine if we share keys per-region.

sre-bot: FYI: GLACIERBANK incident — previous escape-hatch lacked traceability and was misused. We need stronger audit trails and alerts.

jules: UX note: console should show an 'issue bailout' modal with consequences (latency/cost delta) and require manager approval for customers >30k qps. Also show who requested + approval chain.

ashok: Agreed. Policy: bailouts auto-expire at 30m unless extended via the approval workflow. Ops can extend but every extend creates an immutable audit event.

security: We need a threat model doc. If org-admins can create near-immutable overrides, we must have revocation keys, emergency revoke flows, and SIEM/IDS alerts hooked up.

ashok: Plan: write RFC covering token schema, validation library to embed in the proxy, console modal mockups, and an audit webhook. Target: 2-week alpha in staging behind a feature flag.

ryan: any runtime implications? e.g. do we need to bypass model-variant selection or quantization paths? That could be painful if it requires kernel work.

eng-runtime-bot: Note: runtime rule proposed — if `bailout.anchor` present, route -> `stable-v1` variant and disable shard-multiplexing for that request. This will be logged as `bailout.routing_action`.

maria: Telemetry: add `bailout_reason` and `bailout_anchor` dimensions, link to trace_id + org_id, and roll up daily. Also emit an alert if >5% traffic uses a bailout for more than 2h.

product: Product confirms: default allowed requestors are SSO org_admins + support role. Need copy for modal explaining that bailouts DO NOT bypass quotas or billing.

ashok: Important: bailouts are routing-only. They must not increase quotas or bypass rate limits. We'll enforce quota checks prior to routing.

katie: :thumbsup: I'll add pilot list work to the console backlog and coordinate mocks with design. Also add e2e tests for expired tokens and malformed signatures.

ryan: one more safety: bailouts should not be eligible for auto-canary rollout. They should be explicit and logged.

maria: I'll draft the signed JWT spec + small verification lib (python + go). Sample idea for payload: `{"id":"uuid","org":"org-id","exp":<epoch_s>,"reason":"incident-xxxxx","aud":"redwood-bailout"}` and signed with per-region key.

ashok: thanks all. I'll open the RFC and link it here with proposed ACL table and migration checklist. Planning pilot with two enterprise customers behind a feature-flag.

ashok: next steps: (1) security produce threat model, (2) runtime sketch a minimal check, (3) console produce modal mock + approval flow, (4) telemetry add dims/alerts. I'll ping folks in PR.

maria: tagging `@ryan @katie` — I'll post the initial spec in the RFC once done.

katie: bringing this to tomorrow's eng-platform sync for a 10-min decision item.

ashok: perfect. thanks everyone.
